why: Removes the published "a typical first build runs 100-150 credits" figure from every live post. Not replaced with another number: lib/credits.ts estimateCredits() says the two measurements we have are ~144 and ~472 credits, so the published range understates the observed high by more than 3x. On a product whose headline promise is no bill shock, quoting low and charging high is the one direction it must never be wrong in. Sufficiency claims derived from the figure ("enough for a first build plus several rounds of edits") are removed with it — they inherit the same bad arithmetic.

edits.find: Credits don't expire. A typical first build runs roughly 100–150 credits, and a follow-up change is usually in the same range, so the free tier is enough to actually build and iterate on something before you have to decide whether to pay.
edits.replace: Credits don't expire. What a build costs is metered from its real model usage rather than charged as a flat fee, and a build that fails to compile is never charged at all — so you can start building before deciding whether to pay.
edits.note: Metered-not-flat is lib/credits.ts costMicros(); zero-on-failure is creditsCharged: 0 on the FAILED branch of app/api/generate/route.ts.
